summary: This note is a clipped page from the University of Washington IVE help documentation explaining how to write output files in netCDF format for loading into IVE. It describes creating a CDL (network Common data form Description Language) text file, converting it to binary netCDF with the ncgen command, and then appending the main data arrays from a FORTRAN program using ncopn, ncvid, ncvpt1 and ncvpt. A complete example FORTRAN program (netCDF_example1) generates a CDL file, converts it, and writes dummy data for variable A and the time coordinate over seven time steps.
one_line: Help page on writing netCDF output from FORTRAN for IVE, covering CDL files, ncgen conversion, and a complete example program.
key_facts: All data loaded into IVE must be in netCDF (network Common Data Form) format.
A CDL (network Common data form Description Language) file is an ASCII description of the binary data in a netCDF file that is designed to be easily read by humans.
The command ncdump -c sample.nc generates the file sample.cdl containing the file name, dimensions, variable specifications, attributes and coordinate variable data.
The command ncgen -o sample.nc sample.cdl converts the CDL file sample.cdl to the netCDF file sample.nc.
The example CDL file is named implicit_grid and has dimensions lon = 101, lat = 101, level = 5, and time = UNLIMITED (7 currently).
The variable A is declared as float A(time,level,lat,lon) with units "meters/second", and level has units "millibars".
The global attributes include x_min = -180.f, x_max = 180.f, y_min = -90.f, y_max = 90.f, with x_label "longitude" and y_label "latitude".
The level coordinate values are 1000, 850, 700, 500, 300, and the time coordinate values are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12.
The FORTRAN example writes the header to a CDL file named my.cdl, converts it with ncgen, and then opens the file with ncopn for further data input.
The UNLIMITED option for the time dimension allows data to be written at an arbitrary number of output times.
The data written to A in the FORTRAN example are completely artificial dummy values.
The FORTRAN example includes netcdf.inc from /usr/local/include, with the path noted as valid for UW Unix machines.
The page is linked from the IVE Data Format help page, which describes the sample netCDF files used by the default IVE transforms.
